question: You will see one image. Which of these is it most likely to be? (a) a frame from a top-budget film, a AAA game cinematic or a cinema nature documentary, (b) a stock photograph, (c) a seed catalog or textbook picture, (d) amateur generated art, (e) a real-time web 3D demo. Answer with one letter, a confidence from 0 to 100, and the one thing that most influenced your answer.

votes.answer: a, 78/100. The strongest cue was the cinematic low-angle backlighting, with selective rim light separating the foreground sunflowers from the dark field.
e, 92 — The low-poly, faceted 3D geometry of the foreground sunflower leaves alongside hundreds of identically instanced flower and grass meshes across a flat ground plane.

(e), confidence 45. The deciding factor was the field itself: it's thousands of copies of the same sunflower, all the same size and facing the same way. The two plants in front are simple and sparsely modeled, and the grass and sky look like a shader. That points to a real-time scene built from repeated copies, not real photography or film-grade CG. The cinematic color grading and light rays make (a) the runner-up.
e, 85/100. The same sunflower models appear to repeat across the field.
(e) 78. Polygonal leaf edges, flat alpha-card petals, and screen-space god rays look like a real-time web 3D foliage demo, not a film or photo.
